title: Quantum-Limited Symbol-Blind Channel Estimation for Coherent State Discrimination
authors: Hongxu Chen, Renzhi Yuan, Haifeng Yao, Mugen Peng
abstract: Residual dispersion breaks temporal-mode matching in photon-starved coherent links. For equiprobable $M$-ary PSK coherent states in a known spectral mode, with unknown symbols and carrier phase, we establish the quantum limit for blind joint estimation of group delay and second-order dispersion: after eliminating the common phase, it is $4N_s\mathbf{C}$, set by the covariance of the centered generators alone. A multi-output quantum pulse gate with photon-number-resolving detection locally attains it and supports reception below the standard quantum limit under turbulent fading.
summary: This paper develops a quantum-enhanced technique for estimating channel impairments like dispersion and delay in low-photon-number optical links. By employing a Quantum Pulse Gate with photon-number resolution, the authors show that they can achieve measurement precision limited only by fundamental quantum noise, surpassing classical bounds.
main_problem: The primary goal is establishing the quantum limit for blind joint estimation of group delay ($	au$) and second-order dispersion ($\kappa$) in photon-starved coherent optical links.
main_result: A Quantum Pulse Gate (QPG) combined with Photon-Number-Resolving Detectors (PNRDs) measurement locally attains the Quantum Cramér–Rao Bound, achieving performance below the Standard Quantum Limit (SQL).
method: The analysis uses quantum estimation theory, deriving the effective Quantum Fisher Information matrix by exploiting parity decomposition and eliminating unknown common carrier phases via a Schur complement.
model_or_system: The system models coherent state discrimination in fiber links suffering from residual dispersion. The measurement setup involves projecting the field onto phase-diverse temporal modes using a QPG followed by PNRD detection.
key_observables: Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) matrix, error probabilities ($P_e$), and the covariance matrix $C$ of centered generators.
important_parameters: Average photon number ($N_s$), residual dispersion ($\kappa$), group delay ($	au$), and detector efficiency ($\eta_d$).
main_assumptions: The analysis neglects third-order dispersion, assumes equiprobable M-ary PSK states, and utilizes the Schur complement to eliminate unknown common phase dependence.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the proposed temporal-mode-assisted receiver setup and compare error probabilities for different mode-recovery strategies under simulated residual dispersion, showing performance below the SQL.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical problem (dispersion in coherent links) to deriving the QCRB using quantum measurement theory. It details the construction of the optimal QPG/PNRD measurement and concludes by demonstrating that this method surpasses classical limits for blind parameter estimation.
why_interesting: This work directly applies advanced quantum information techniques (QFI, POVMs) to a practical problem in quantum communication (optical fiber links), providing concrete bounds on achievable sensing precision below the SQL.
